conbody.p: If you leave your devices unattended while in public you increase the risk of theft for your devices or access to your devices.
If you leave your devices in your office, lock it up when you leave. Leaving it unlocked increases the risk of theft.
If you step away from your screen at any point, lock your device. Leaving it unlocked allows the opportunity for someone else to use your account.

People will often upload malware onto physical devices as a way to try to get access to systems. If you install a thumb drive into your computer and you do not trust it completely, there is a risk that it is a thumb drive with malware on it.

Sometimes there are publicly available USB ports to charge your device. Some threat actors hijack these outlets in order to upload malware or download your data, so install a data blocker on your device to prevent the transference of data, while allowing you to still charge your device.

When getting rid of an old device, either store it in a safe location, remove the encrypted harddrive, or go to a professional destruction facility that can offer a certificate of destruction. This will protect the data that was on these devices.
